audit.why: Win rate 59.11% over 1636 games, Vladimir-favored by data.
Early lane is Swain's (Nevermove root, fragment sustain); Vladimir takes over at first item and scales harder. diff EVEN 5.5/10 is defensible given the 59% WR leans Vladimir.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..5].side are a blanket 'Skill' while content win[] and the packet chart both give Swain levels 1-6 and Vladimir from first item — two answers to the same question on one page.
audit.why: Content chart is grounded: Swain's Nevermove (E, 12s) into Death's Hand (Q, 7s scaling to 3s) plus Ravenous Flock fragments beats early Vladimir; Demonic Ascension out-drains the level-6 all-in; Riftmaker flips the sustain war.
audit.corrected: phases[0..5].side moved to match content win[]; whys and ratings rewritten to match each verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text labels Nevermove as (W) and Vision of Empire as (E) — slots are swapped. Nevermove is Swain's E, Vision of Empire is his W.
audit.why: Riot kit file: E = Nevermove (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, 850 range, root on return, pull), W = Vision of Empire (22-18s, global-ish range, slow+reveal). Sanguine Pool dodges the Nevermove return root; Swain P/R healing makes Grievous Wounds timing matter (missingInteractions).
audit.corrected: Slots corrected in spikes[0].text; cooldown numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns; anti-heal already covered in report[8].

audit.why: Nevermove 12s rank 1, Demonic Ascension 120s, Vladimir W 28s early — the numbers make the windows concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad under unrelated titles (copy-paste bleed).
audit.why: Lint findings; bodies now explain their own titles from Swain's kit.

Sanguine Pool untargetability dodges Nevermove's return root and the Hemoplague-vs-Ascension drain race are the hidden decision points; both now stated on-page. Spell-shield/cleanse specifics for Nevermove are not in the kit text — not asserted.
No 26.15 change to either kit that moves this matchup; not verified against patch notes beyond the kit data.

edits.before: Q-farm and nothing else — your level 1 is among the worst mid. Give CS you can't Q safely and smile about it.
edits.after: His Death's Hand pierces the wave to poke you for free — Q-farm at 600 range and give CS you cannot take safely.

edits.before: Still surviving. Q on cooldown when free, pool saved for the jungler you haven't seen yet.
edits.after: Nevermove arrives at 2 — dodge the returning root or the Q follow-up chunks a quarter bar.

edits.before: E charges join the pattern: Q-E wave contact trades start mattering. Health is your mana — spend like an accountant.
edits.after: His full root-into-Q pattern is online and his fragments outheal your Transfusion — trade only after Nevermove whiffs.

edits.before: The crimson rush timing — Q empowers every third-ish cast and the sustain war starts tilting your way.
edits.after: He banks fragments and his Q cooldown keeps falling — your crimson-rush Qs narrow it, he still wins poke.

edits.before: Hemoplague online — the all-in inverts: Q-E-R-E with ignite kills most mids who thought they were winning.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension out-drains your Hemoplague all-in — do not test his 6; wait for the 120s cooldown or your item.

edits.before: Riftmaker timing: every trade heals more than it costs. Extended fights are now donations to your health bar.
edits.after: Riftmaker flips the drain war — you outheal him outside Demonic Ascension and pool the Nevermove that starts kills.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. It governs your forward steps. - W Sanguine Pool spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 — when it whiffs, that is your trade window. Demonic Ascension is 120s and lasts while he drains champions: disengage, reset, and fight the two-minute downtime. Your pool is 28s early — never spend it on poke you can heal back.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: Nevermove only roots on its return — sidestep the comeback or pool it, and his one 12-second setup spell is gone.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: Charging E inside his 850-range Nevermove line at half HP hands him the root, the pull, and the Q bolts — charge from fog or after his E whiffs.

edits.before: Swain wins by landing Demonic Ascension, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Swain wins by landing Nevermove's return root, stacking Death's Hand bolts, and out-draining you in Demonic Ascension.

edits.before: Swain wins the early lane: Nevermove (W) into Death's Hand (Q) roots and chunks you, and his passive soul fragments plus Vision of Empire (E) let him sustain and poke through your Transfusion.
edits.after: Swain wins the early lane: Nevermove (E) into Death's Hand (Q) roots and chunks you, and his passive soul fragments plus Vision of Empire (W) let him sustain and poke through your Transfusion.

notes: Packet defect flags the chart contradicting the 59.11% Vladimir win rate; the chart is still credible — Vladimir's WR comes from post-item scaling while Swain genuinely owns levels 1-6 (Nevermove/fragments/Ascension). Content win[] left untouched; full sides aligned to it per the chart rule.
